text.p: Singapore plans to put teachers in police uniform to help combat juvenile delinquency.
A scheme outlined by Minister of State for Law and Home Affairs Ho Peng Kee at the weekend would give teacher volunteers training to become special constables.
They would be allowed to wear police uniform and would exercise some police powers when a pilot programme starts in August, Ho said in a speech.
He said police and schools needed to cooperate to combat rising juvenile crime in Singapore, where some offenders can be caned.
"The number of juveniles arrested increased from 1,374 cases in 1986 to 2,101 in 1996. Juvenile delinquency is unacceptably high. It must be reduced," Ho said.
The Singapore Teachers' Union (STU) gave a cautious welcome to the plan on Monday.
Swithun Lowe, STU deputy general secretary, told Reuters the plans appeared to be based on proposals the union made after a 1995 trip to Australia, where a similar scheme operated.
"I think we will monitor how the experiment goes and see how it will work compared to our original proposal," Lowe said.
The STU plan sought the appointment of trained, uniformed police officers to schools where they would act as counsellors and teach road safety and basic law and order as part of the curriculum.
Lowe said the distinction between being a trained police officer and receiving police training was important to the success of the scheme.
"If the teachers chosen are also trained police officers and good counsellors then it might help the scheme to work," he said.
